raw_empirical_output_as_emitted_before_r.note: These emitted classification counts are preserved as failed V1 output only. They are not scientifically accepted because artifact inspection identified implementation/source-semantics defects that invalidate the classifications.

artifact_review_failures.finding: The raw first-party inactive pages contain machine-readable JSON-LD datePublished timestamps with UTC offsets, but V1 did not parse them and instead reduced visible same-day publication strings to date-only chronology.
concrete_examples: Chiefs Week 10 inactive raw source S016 contains datePublished=2021-11-15T00:01:57.189Z, before the frozen 2021-11-15T01:20:00Z kickoff, but V1 rejected Khalen Saunders as same_day_date_without_ordering.

Buccaneers Week 10 inactive raw source S018 contains datePublished=2021-11-14T16:30:00Z, before the frozen 2021-11-14T18:00:00Z kickoff, but V1 rejected the explicit Antonio Brown inactive designation as same_day_date_without_ordering.

Steelers Week 16 inactive raw source S021 contains datePublished=2021-12-26T19:55:00Z, before the frozen 2021-12-26T21:25:00Z kickoff, but V1 rejected the explicit Chris Wormley inactive designation as same_day_date_without_ordering.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: V1 same-day chronology classifications are not reliable.

artifact_review_failures.finding: V1 could preserve NOT_APPLICABLE_NOT_ROSTER_ELIGIBLE from an older waived/practice-squad event after a later explicit activation/elevation changed roster eligibility.
artifact_review_failures.concrete_example: Doug Middleton was emitted as PROVABLY_ROSTER_ELIGIBLE_BEFORE_KICKOFF while simultaneously retaining NOT_APPLICABLE_NOT_ROSTER_ELIGIBLE after later activation/elevation events. This state pair is internally inconsistent and violates the intended ordered-event taxonomy.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: Any V1 row depending on multi-event state reduction is scientifically invalid.

artifact_review_failures.finding: The source corpus contains standard-elevation events that are explicitly temporary/game-scoped. V1 treated ELEVATED_ACTIVATED as a general terminal roster state without proving that an elevation applied to the target game or persisted through the target kickoff.
artifact_review_failures.concrete_example: Doug Middleton has explicit Jacksonville standard-elevation/activation chronology before Week 11, including events tied to earlier games. V1 lacked a frozen target-game applicability rule, so those events cannot safely establish Week 11 kickoff eligibility.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: A successor must distinguish permanent active-roster transactions from temporary standard elevations and require target-game applicability for the latter.

artifact_review_failures.finding: V1 could carry an old roster state forward to the target kickoff merely because no later qualifying transaction was parsed. That requires a separately qualified completeness/persistence premise and conflicts with the frozen rule that source absence is non-evidence.
concrete_examples: Mike Glennon was emitted as PRACTICE_SQUAD for November and December targets from September 4-5 waiver/practice-squad events without a target-game-specific source proving that state at those kickoffs.

Antonio Brown was emitted as a reserve/non-eligible state from a September reserve/COVID transaction even though the same transaction ledger contains a September 29 activation and the target-game inactive page explicitly designates him inactive in November.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: A successor may not project stale roster states through target kickoff unless source completeness and state persistence are explicitly frozen and justified.

artifact_review_failures.finding: Generic reserve/injury language in a broad article context could be attributed to the target player even when it described a different player.
artifact_review_failures.concrete_example: The Buccaneers inactive article contains Antonio Brown in the inactive list and separately discusses Montez Sweat on injured reserve; V1 produced a reserve-style event for Brown from broad context. Player-local clause/list parsing must be stricter in any successor.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: V1 article-context roster classifications are not accepted.

artifact_review_failures.finding: V1 recognized placement on reserve/COVID but did not symmetrically recognize activation from reserve/COVID as an eligibility-restoring event.
artifact_review_failures.concrete_example: The Buccaneers transaction ledger includes Antonio Brown activated from the reserve/COVID-19 list on 2021-09-29 after placement on 2021-09-21; V1 retained the older reserve state.
artifact_review_failures.disposition: V1 terminal roster state for affected reserve/activation sequences is invalid.

scientific_interpretation.reason: The raw artifact is valuable preserved evidence, but post-run inspection falsified the V1 implementation as a defensible interpreter of that evidence. Under the frozen fail-closed rules, the experiment is archived as failed rather than patched or reinterpreted in-place.

successor_constraints: Start a separately preregistered V2; do not mutate the V1 frozen contract or reinterpret V1 output as qualified.
Parse machine-readable source publication timestamps, including JSON-LD datePublished, before falling back to visible date text.
Use a player-local evidence grammar for every source class; neighboring-player reserve/injury language cannot classify the target.
Use ordered-event reduction that clears stale non-eligibility designations when an explicit later eligibility-restoring event occurs.
Distinguish permanent active-roster transactions from standard elevations and require explicit target-game applicability for temporary elevations.
Do not project stale transaction states to kickoff from absence of later changes unless a separately preregistered completeness/persistence premise is qualified.
Continue to leave unresolved chronology unresolved; do not use weekly status, source absence, postgame participation, or manual exceptions as rescue evidence.
